title: Metformin and metformin-containing medicines: Article 31 referral. Use of metformin to treat diabetes now expanded to patients with moderately reduced kidney function
journal: European Medicines Agency, reference EMA/603690/2016, first published 14 October 2016
funder: European Medicines Agency; review initiated at the request of the Netherlands
result: The review was initiated on 28 January 2016 at the request of the Netherlands under Article 31 of Directive 2001/83/EC. On 13 October 2016 the Agency concluded that metformin-containing medicines can be used in patients with moderately reduced kidney function (glomerular filtration rate 30 to 59 ml/min), revising the previous contraindication; use remains contraindicated below 30 ml/min. GFR is to be assessed before starting treatment and at least annually thereafter, and reduced doses considered in moderate reduction. The product information was also to detail risk factors for lactic acidosis to be reviewed before and during treatment, and to advise patients to stop metformin for a short time and seek advice when dehydrated through severe vomiting, diarrhoea, fever, heat exposure or reduced fluid intake. Companies marketing metformin-containing medicines were requested to monitor and analyse future lactic acidosis cases and report them in periodic safety reviews. Several fixed-dose combinations remain not recommended in moderately reduced kidney function because of the second active substance. The Agency lists among the evidence considered Eppenga et al., Diabetes Care 2014;37(8):2218; Richy et al., Diabetes Care 2014;37(8):2291; and Salpeter et al., Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2010, CD002967.
